newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia urges tighter tax screw on foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Russia urges tighter tax screw on foreign firms.

text.p: Russia must take tough measures against foreign firms in arrears or not paying taxes, a State Tax Service official said on Thursday.

"The time has come to take the most severe measures in relation to violators of tax law and those in arrears," Vladimir Oskin, deputy head of the administration for foreign tax relations, told a news conference.
Foreign firms working in Russia say Russia's complex tax system is harsh, arbitrarily enforced and includes taxes unheard of in their home countries, such as taxes on advertising.
But Oskin said foreign firms have it easy compared with Russian companies, who he said pay taxes quarterly or monthly on profits not yet made.
"The main reason for the wild growth in the number of foreign firms working in Russia is that foreign juridical entities have significant tax advantages compared to Russian enterprises," he said.

Oskin said 9,000 foreign firms registered with the State Tax Service in 1996, 3,000 of them for the first time, and paid over two trillion roubles ($400 million) in taxes in 1996, 2.3 times more than in 1995.
But he said foreign firms owed Russia a total of over $74 million as of March 1 this year.
"I want to say, with great regret, that we have wonderful conditions for foreign companies to break Russian tax law," Oskin said.
Oskin said outdated systems for accrediting foreign companies and weak sanctions against offenders should be overhauled and he called for criminal cases against violators.
He also called for the revokation of a long-standing double-taxation agreement with Cyprus.
"It's no accident that every fourth foreign firm registered in Moscow is Cypriot," said Oskin.
"The mind boggles why we don't denounce this agreement which is causing us huge tax losses," he said.

The Russian government is drawing up a plan of massive budget spending cuts due to dismal tax collection rates. Different estimates put real tax collection rates for the first quarter of 1997 at between 39 percent and 49 percent of targets.
Official figures showed total tax arrears at the beginning of the year were $23 billion (128.25 trillion roubles).
